title: The Cup of Tea That Left a Radioactive Trail

narration: A man drank tea in a London hotel bar.
Three weeks later, he was dead.
Investigators found the teapot was radioactive.
shots.visual_description: lt14 hotel bar (night grade); lt14_guest (silhouette): sit -> sit_type -> sit -> sit_slumped; lt14_tech (silhouette): torch -> torch_low -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'LONDON · NOVEMBER 2006', label 'THREE WEEKS LATER', svg, callout 'THE TEAPOT'.

sources.claim_text: At the Pine Bar meeting on 1 November 2006 Litvinenko drank green tea from the pot; the two other men had gin.
On 1 November 2006 Litvinenko met Andrei Lugovoi and Dmitry Kovtun at the Pine Bar of the Millennium Hotel, Grosvenor Square, London.
Litvinenko died in London on 23 November 2006.

After Litvinenko's death, investigators surveyed the Millennium Hotel's Pine Bar for polonium-210 contamination; the contamination map ran from lower readings across the bar to the highest at the table where the group sat.

The highest readings in the bar came from the teapot Litvinenko drank from (the largest reading from its spout), as described in reporting on the 2016 inquiry; the inquiry released images of the teapot.

narration: Alexander Litvinenko. Former Russian security officer. Kremlin critic.
shots.visual_description: lt14 london night (night grade); lt14_guest (silhouette): stand -> stand -> hands_together (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'ALEXANDER LITVINENKO', label 'KREMLIN CRITIC'.

sources.claim_text: Alexander Litvinenko was a former officer of Russia's FSB security service who came to Britain in 2000, became a prominent Kremlin critic, and lived in London.

narration: November 1st, 2006: he had met two Russian men there.
That night, he fell ill.
shots.visual_description: lt14 hotel bar (night grade); lt14_visitor_b (silhouette): sit -> sit_slumped -> sit; lt14_guest (silhouette): sit -> sit_type -> sit -> stand (walks); lt14_visitor_a (silhouette): sit -> sit_read -> sit; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '1 NOV 2006 · THE PINE BAR'.

sources.claim_text: On 1 November 2006 Litvinenko met Andrei Lugovoi and Dmitry Kovtun at the Pine Bar of the Millennium Hotel, Grosvenor Square, London.
Litvinenko fell ill on 1 November 2006 and was taken to hospital.

narration: For three weeks, doctors couldn't name the poison.
Hours before he died, scientists found it.
It was polonium-210.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); scientist (silhouette): examine -> read -> examine -> point -> hand_to_face; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '1-23 NOVEMBER 2006', card 'IDENTIFIED · 23 NOVEMBER 2006 / POLONIUM-210 / RARE · RADIOACTIVE / HE DIED HOURS LATER'.

overlays.text: IDENTIFIED · 23 NOVEMBER 2006 / POLONIUM-210 / RARE · RADIOACTIVE / HE DIED HOURS LATER

sources.claim_text: For about three weeks the cause of his illness was not identified: the early clinical picture resembled infection or chemical poisoning such as thallium.

Polonium-210 was identified only hours before he died (NBC: about two hours; EUvsDisinfo: six hours after the urine result); the Health Protection Agency announced it on 24 November. Polonium-210 is described as a rare, radioactive element.

narration: Its radiation can't even get through skin.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst (silhouette): sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit; agent_b (silhouette): torch -> torch_low -> torch -> torch_low; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: funfact 'Its alpha radiation is stopped / by a thin layer of skin. / Finding it takes special detectors.'.

overlays.text: Its alpha radiation is stopped / by a thin layer of skin. / Finding it takes special detectors.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: polonium-210 emits alpha radiation, which is stopped by a thin layer of matter such as skin; ordinary Geiger counters pick up beta and gamma radiation, and alpha radiation needs special detectors (Aldermaston identified it by its 5.3 MeV alpha signature).

narration: They traced it across London: a sushi bar, offices, his home.
Even Arsenal's stadium, where the two men watched a match.
shots.visual_description: lt14 trail map (night grade); detective (silhouette): stand -> point -> point_up -> arms_crossed -> point_up -> stand; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: funfact 'Traces turned up at Arsenal's / Emirates Stadium. Health officials: / "barely detectable", no public risk.'.

overlays.text: Traces turned up at Arsenal's / Emirates Stadium. Health officials: / "barely detectable", no public risk.

sources.claim_text: Investigators traced polonium contamination to sites across London, including the Itsu sushi restaurant near Piccadilly, an office block and a Mayfair address, and Litvinenko's north London home; by 30 November traces had been found at 12 sites, and dozens of scenes were assessed.

Two British Airways Boeing 767s at Heathrow showed traces of radioactive material at very low levels (late November 2006); officials did not then say whether it was polonium-210, and the health risk was called low.

FUN FACT: traces of polonium-210 were found at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, where Lugovoi and Kovtun watched Arsenal v CSKA Moscow on the evening of 1 November 2006; the Health Protection Agency called the levels barely detectable and no risk to the public.

narration: And the hottest spot? The teapot.
shots.visual_description: lt14 hotel bar (night grade); lt14_tech (silhouette): torch -> torch_low -> stand_tense; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, callout 'HIGHEST READINGS'.

sources.claim_text: The highest readings in the bar came from the teapot Litvinenko drank from (the largest reading from its spout), as described in reporting on the 2016 inquiry; the inquiry released images of the teapot.

narration: Britain charged Lugovoi with murder.
Russia refused to extradite him.
shots.visual_description: courthouse night (night grade); official (silhouette): read -> stand -> hands_together (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'UK PROSECUTORS · MAY 2007 / CHARGED WITH MURDER: / ANDREI LUGOVOI', stamp 'EXTRADITION REFUSED', label 'RUSSIA · JULY 2007'.

overlays.text: UK PROSECUTORS · MAY 2007 / CHARGED WITH MURDER: / ANDREI LUGOVOI

sources.claim_text: In May 2007 the Director of Public Prosecutions said there was sufficient evidence to charge Andrei Lugovoi with Litvinenko's murder, and Britain requested his extradition.
On 5 July 2007 Russia formally refused to extradite Lugovoi, citing article 61 of its constitution (a Russian citizen cannot be handed over to another state).

narration: In 2016, a UK public inquiry concluded Lugovoi and Dmitry Kovtun poisoned him.
Probably approved, it said, by President Putin and FSB chief Patrushev.
shots.visual_description: press room (cold grade); official (silhouette): read -> present -> read -> hands_together -> present; press_operator (silhouette): read -> stand_tense -> read -> hand_to_face; keyed camera moves; overlays: card 'UK PUBLIC INQUIRY · JANUARY 2016 / CONCLUDED: / LUGOVOI AND KOVTUN / POISONED HIM', card 'IT SAID: "PROBABLY APPROVED" / BY PRESIDENT PUTIN / AND FSB CHIEF PATRUSHEV / INQUIRY FINDINGS · NOT A CRIMINAL VERDICT'.

overlays.text: UK PUBLIC INQUIRY · JANUARY 2016 / CONCLUDED: / LUGOVOI AND KOVTUN / POISONED HIM
IT SAID: "PROBABLY APPROVED" / BY PRESIDENT PUTIN / AND FSB CHIEF PATRUSHEV / INQUIRY FINDINGS · NOT A CRIMINAL VERDICT

sources.claim_text: The UK public inquiry chaired by Sir Robert Owen reported on 21 January 2016 that Lugovoi and Kovtun deliberately poisoned Litvinenko with polonium-210 at the Pine Bar on 1 November 2006 (placing it in the teapot), probably under the direction of the FSB. This is an inquiry finding, not a criminal verdict; neither man has been tried.
The inquiry concluded that the FSB operation to kill Litvinenko was 'probably approved' by Nikolai Patrushev, then director of the FSB, and also by President Putin.

narration: Both men denied it.
Kovtun died in 2022.
Russia denies any role.
shots.visual_description: lt14 london night (night grade); press_operator (silhouette): read -> stand -> read (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'LUGOVOI: DENIES IT / KOVTUN: DENIED IT · DIED 2022 / RUSSIA: DENIES ANY ROLE'.

overlays.text: LUGOVOI: DENIES IT / KOVTUN: DENIED IT · DIED 2022 / RUSSIA: DENIES ANY ROLE

sources.claim_text: Lugovoi has denied any involvement since 2007, calling the accusations politically motivated, and disputed the 2016 findings; Kovtun also denied it (in 2015 he suggested the death was an accident).
Dmitry Kovtun died in Moscow in June 2022 (reported as COVID-19, citing TASS).
Russia rejected the inquiry's findings and denies involvement; its ambassador called the inquiry a 'blatant provocation'.

narration: In 2021, the European Court of Human Rights held Russia responsible.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); judge (silhouette): sit -> sit_read -> sit; judge (silhouette): sit -> sit_read -> sit; judge (silhouette): sit -> sit_read -> sit; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'EUROPEAN COURT OF HUMAN RIGHTS / 21 SEPTEMBER 2021 · CARTER v RUSSIA / RUSSIA RESPONSIBLE / FOR THE KILLING'.

overlays.text: EUROPEAN COURT OF HUMAN RIGHTS / 21 SEPTEMBER 2021 · CARTER v RUSSIA / RUSSIA RESPONSIBLE / FOR THE KILLING

sources.claim_text: On 21 September 2021 the European Court of Human Rights (Carter v Russia) held Russia responsible for Litvinenko's killing, finding a strong prima facie case that Lugovoi and Kovtun acted as agents of the Russian state.

narration: Twenty years on, no one has stood trial.
It all comes back to one teapot.
Which case next?

sources.claim_text: Litvinenko died on 23 November 2006: November 2026 marks 20 years (this episode is published in October 2026).

No one has been tried for Litvinenko's death: Russia refused extradition, Kovtun died in 2022, and no trial or new legal step was found on 2026-10-11 (Lugovoi remains under UK sanctions, notice amended March 2025).

The highest readings in the bar came from the teapot Litvinenko drank from (the largest reading from its spout), as described in reporting on the 2016 inquiry; the inquiry released images of the teapot.
